name: Gauss Flechette Repeater GFR-3 'Needlerain'
description:
The GFR-3 operates on stacked linear magnetic acceleration coils arranged in a helical configuration, cycling sub-caliber tungsten-ceramic flechettes at approximately 4,200 rounds per minute. Each flechette — roughly 3mm wide and 22mm long — is ferromagnetically coated along its rear third, allowing the coil stack to grab, accelerate, and release in under 0.8 milliseconds per round. The result is a nearly silent, caseless stream of kinetic penetrators that can saturate a doorframe-sized area at close range or punch through light armor panels at distance.

What distinguishes the GFR-3 from earlier gauss repeaters is its adaptive coil timing system, which reads barrel temperature and magnetic field saturation 200 times per second and adjusts current delivery to maintain consistent muzzle velocity even as the barrel heats. Earlier models suffered from 'velocity drift,' where rounds fired late in a magazine were significantly slower than initial rounds, producing inconsistent terminal performance. The GFR-3 solved this through TESSERA CORPONATION's proprietary FluxSync firmware, which also enables selectable dispersion patterns — tight column for armor penetration, wide fan for crowd suppression.

The weapon uses a 300-round cassette magazine that sits beneath the barrel in a bullpup configuration, giving the GFR-3 a stubby, aggressive silhouette. It has no mechanical action, no ejection port, and minimal moving parts beyond the cassette feed mechanism, which makes it exceptionally reliable in wet or contaminated environments. The lack of a traditional trigger group — replaced by a capacitive palm sensor and a pressure ring around the grip — means the weapon cannot fire if not held correctly, a feature that has made it popular with corporate security who worry about weapon retention.
specifications:
caliber: 3x22mm tungsten-ceramic flechette
feed system: 300-round sealed cassette, electromagnetic advancement
rate of fire: 4,200 RPM (cyclic), adjustable to 800 RPM semi-burst
effective range: 12m (fan dispersion), 180m (column mode)
muzzle velocity: 1,050 m/s nominal (FluxSync maintained)
weight: 2.8 kg loaded
dimensions: 410mm length, 240mm height
power source: Integrated 18V lithium-polymer cell, 6 cassettes per charge
operating temperature: -20°C to +65°C
tactical_use: Corporate security teams use the GFR-3 primarily in column mode for breaching armored targets at short-to-medium range, switching to fan dispersion for room clearing or crowd control. Its silence — the loudest component is the faint magnetic hum and the impact of flechettes — makes it favored for operations where noise discipline matters. The 300-round cassette allows sustained suppressive fire without reloads, though operators are trained to swap cassettes at 150 rounds to avoid feed jams from heat buildup in the advancement mechanism. Some operators tape two cassettes together for rapid exchange.
cultural_context: The GFR-3 carries a specific social weight in GLMZ: it is the weapon of the corporate floor. Seen holstered on TESSERA's own lobby security and licensed to a dozen mid-tier corporate clients, the 'Needlerain' is understood as a statement of institutional violence — clean, efficient, calibrated. Street gangs rarely carry them because the cassette magazines are expensive and proprietary. When one appears outside a corporate context, it usually means someone raided a security depot or a corporate operative has gone freelance. The weapon's silence gives it a particular dread reputation in the lower arcologies, where the first sign of a GFR-3 in the room is often the sound of someone else getting hit.
known_users: Black market arms dealers (stolen units only)
story_hooks: A GFR-3 cassette recovered from a crime scene is stamped with a TESSERA internal security lot number — meaning it came from inside the building, not from outside
The FluxSync firmware update pushed to all GFR-3 units contains a hidden killswitch that TESSERA can activate remotely, and someone has just discovered this
A weapons tech claims to have cracked the cassette format and is producing third-party flechette loads — TESSERA wants her silenced before the patent violation goes public
An operator whose GFR-3 malfunctioned during a job is suing TESSERA, and the trial is threatening to expose classified use cases for the weapon

physical_description.visual_profile: Aggressively compact bullpup platform with a subtly menacing stance. The GFR-3 reads as purposefully engineered rather than organic — all hard angles, recessed surfaces, and integrated subsystems. The stubby barrel is almost vestigial, dwarfed by the prominent 300-round cassette mounted beneath like a secondary fuselage. Overall impression: a precision tool designed for controlled lethality.
physical_description.dimensions: 410mm overall length, 240mm height. Barrel section roughly 120mm. Magazine cassette extends 180mm beneath the receiver, giving it a top-heavy visual weight.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and purposeful in hand at 2.8kg loaded — not feather-light, but distributed in a way that feels intentional rather than burdensome. The cassette's weight sits low, creating a natural cant toward the operator's body.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite matrix (TESSERA proprietary blend) over a steel coil assembly backbone. Cassette housing is reinforced aluminum with ferromagnetic shielding.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with strategic brushed-steel accent panels where coil arrays interface with the polymer shell. The cassette magazine features a subtle carbon-weave texture visible under certain angles. Minimal reflectivity — designed for low-light operations.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, brushed steel accents, charcoal composite inlays. The capacitive grip ring is offset in a darker anthracite tone with subtle RGB status indicators (blue when dormant, amber during spin-up, red during firing).
physical_description.grip_texture: The pressure-sensitive palm grip is wrapped in micro-textured silicone with reinforced polymer substructure — tacky but not soft, designed to maintain contact through sweat or light contamination. Knurled grip ring for index finger pressure modulation.
distinctive_features: Dual thermal vents running along the rear receiver block — visible heat-dissipation channels that glow faintly amber under heavy fire
Integrated 3-position mode selector marked in Φ-stamped legend: COLUMN, FAN, SAFE
Faint electromagnetic hum induction coils visible as subtle surface ribbing across barrel shroud
Flip-up capacitive readout display mounted on left side showing round count, temperature, and power status in cyan HUD numerals
Four contact pads for external power umbilical (rarely used in field ops)
Subtle TESSERA corporate hexagon logo embossed on the cassette housing, barely raised above surface
Ammunition visibility window on cassette showing ferromagnetic flechette arrangement in stacked columns
Integrated cable management channel along underside of grip for field charging
Faint scorch marks and micro-abrasions typical of operational wear — not pristine, not battle-scarred, but clearly used
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION logotype (hexagon emblem) stamped subtly on the cassette spine. Serial number etched in microfont on a recessed steel plate behind the grip. Model designation GFR-3 printed in tactical sans-serif on the barrel shroud. All markings use low-reflectivity phosphate finish.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-operational. Well-maintained by professional users but showing evidence of repeated use — minor scuff marks on the polymer furniture, faint thermal stress discoloration around the vent channels, slight wear on the grip's micro-texture from gloved handling. Cassette housing shows minor dents consistent with tactical gear contact. No rust or corrosion — TESSERA engineering ensures reliability in GLMZ industrial environments.
